Post 1
ASX closed at 8,310 points last week as USD strength and China demand fears kept a lid on the rally. Mixed signals make this a week to stay selective, not aggressive. The single tension: can domestic resilience offset global headwinds? #ASX #ausbiz

Post 2
🏦 Banks face RBA minutes Tuesday — any hawkish tilt hits mortgage books hard. ⛏️ Miners watch China's October activity data; iron ore held near USD 98/t but the floor looks fragile. Two sectors, two catalysts, one week. #banking #ironore #ASX

Post 3
🔺 Watch the major iron ore producers closely — BHP trades near AUD 43 and any China stimulus signal this week could reprice the whole sector fast. Thin liquidity amplifies the move. #mining #BHP #ASX #ausbiz

Post 4
S&P 500 closed near 5,893 points Friday. USD index above 106 is the real pressure point — it squeezes commodity prices and weighs on ASX resource earnings. If USD holds here, expect headwinds to persist into Wednesday. #ausbiz #ASX #globalmarkets #inflation

Post 5
RBA minutes drop Tuesday. Market prices zero cuts before mid-2026. A hawkish surprise pressures rate-sensitive stocks; a dovish tilt could lift property 2%+. Which way are you positioned — hold, hedge, or buy the dip? #RBA #ausbiz #ASX #property
